Frustratingly, what all three shows have in common is a feeling of paddedness, along with a well-intentioned but half-baked search for a gestural vocabulary beyond straight realism, the results of which haven’t so much cracked open the stories as burdened them with predictable devices.

Essentially a sorrowful drama that concludes on a mildly upbeat note, runboyrun is far more substantial than In Old Age, which is situated some years in the future (and several plays later) in Udofia’s series.
Missing Mfoniso Udofia's plays is missing enormous opportunities for grappling with what it means to be human.
